title: LINQ Method Syntax
description: Learn the fluent method syntax for writing LINQ queries using extension methods.

data.text: Method syntax (also known as **fluent syntax**) uses extension methods included in the `Enumerable` or `Queryable` static class, similar to how you would call any extension method of a class.

data.title: Compilation
data.text: The compiler converts query syntax into method syntax at compile time. Both syntaxes produce the same result.

data.title: Basic Method Syntax

data.text: Method syntax comprises extension methods and lambda expressions. The `Where()` extension method is defined in the `Enumerable` class.

If you check the signature of the `Where` extension method, you will find that it accepts a **predicate delegate** as `Func<TSource, bool>`. This means you can pass any delegate function that accepts an input parameter and returns a Boolean value.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Method syntax uses extension methods and lambda expressions
The compiler converts query syntax to method syntax at compile time
Method syntax allows chaining multiple operations
Some LINQ operators are only available in method syntax
